items.stem: In an operational-level case response, what should most directly shape the content and emphasis of your answer?

options.text: The specific tasks and requirements set in the exam
options.rationale: Correct: marks are awarded for addressing the stated task requirements, so they must drive the response.

options.text: Every topic in the operational-level syllabus
options.rationale: Writing everything you know wastes time and misses marks tied to the actual tasks.

options.text: The longest section of the pre-seen material
options.rationale: Length of pre-seen material does not determine what the tasks require.

options.text: The order in which exhibits appear
options.rationale: Exhibit order is incidental; the task requirements govern the answer.

items.explanation: Correct: marks are awarded for addressing the stated task requirements, so they must drive the response.

items.stem: A case company reports rising revenue but falling operating cash flow. Which analysis is the most relevant first step?

options.text: Examine movements in working capital such as receivables and inventory
options.rationale: Correct: a revenue/cash divergence usually signals working-capital build-up, so examine receivables and inventory first.

options.text: Assume the figures contain an error and ignore them
options.rationale: Dismissing data is not analysis; the divergence is a common, explainable pattern.
Increasing dividends ignores the cash-flow problem and is premature.
A single divergence does not establish insolvency without further analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: a revenue/cash divergence usually signals working-capital build-up, so examine receivables and inventory first.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that improve exam technique in a timed case-study response.

options.text: Allocating time to tasks in proportion to their marks
options.rationale: Correct: proportioning time to marks maximises achievable marks across all tasks.

options.text: Linking recommendations to the specific scenario facts
options.rationale: Correct: scenario-specific application earns application marks over generic statements.

options.text: Writing a long generic essay covering the whole syllabus
options.rationale: Generic coverage ignores the tasks and wastes limited time.

options.text: Leaving the highest-mark task until no time remains
options.rationale: Deprioritising high-mark tasks risks losing the most marks.
Copying the pre-seen adds no analysis and earns no application marks.

items.explanation: Correct: proportioning time to marks maximises achievable marks across all tasks.
